# <span id="aanchor207"></span> Crystal Export Types

The following export formats are available for Crystal reports:

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="CSV">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Character Separated Values (CSV)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="CSV">

This is a record-based export format. Each column is separated by a predefined character called delimiter in the export. If the delimiter used is comma, then it is called comma separated values or CSV. If **TAB** is used, then it is called TabSeparatedText (TTX). This export file can be opened in Excel or Notepad. This is a very popular method for exporting raw reports to Microsoft Excel users.

<div class="example">

**Example:** CommaSeparatedValues, TabSeperatedText

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="RPT">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Crystal Reports (RPT)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="RPT">

This format saves reports as RPT files, which you can open in Visual Studio. The RPT file is saved with the data. This is the same as using the Save As feature with the Save Data with Report option selected.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="RTF">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Rich Text Format (RTF)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="RTF">

This export formats produces RTF files. The EditableRTF option creates files that contain only text and no drawing objects. The RichText option produces files that can contain text and drawing objects. Both files can be opened in word processing programs such as Microsoft Word.

<div class="example">

**Example:** EditableRTF, RichText

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="XLSX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Microsoft Excel (XLSX)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="XLSX">

This produces report in an Excel format. Each column in report corresponds to a column in Excel. The report is exported page-by-page and added to single worksheet with the same name as the report name. If the worksheet becomes full, then the Crystal report will create another worksheet and continue.

If there are more columns in the report than Excel can support, the additional report columns are omitted from the export. The XLS format can only support 256 columns; the XLSX format can handle 16,384 columns. This option also exports report formulas (supported formulas are SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MIN and MAX).

Three export options are available:

- **Microsoft Excel (97-2003) (\*.xls)** - This XLS format corresponds to Microsoft Excel (97-2003) (\*.xls). This is a page-based export option that retains the original formatting, but lines and boxes are omitted from the report.
- **Microsoft Excel (97-2003) Data-Only** - This is a record-based export type. Only the report data is exported; formatting is not included.
- **Microsoft Excel Data-Only (\*.xlsx)** - This is similar to the Microsoft Excel (97-2003) Data-Only format, but it supports more columns.

<div class="example">

**Example:** Excel, ExcelRecord, ExcelWorkbook

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="HTML">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />HTML</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="HTML">

Creates an HTML format that preserves the original report layout. Useful for mailing well formatted reports to customers. Crystal can export to in HTML 3.2 or HTML 4.0.

<div class="example">

**Example:** HTML32, HTML40

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="PDF">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />PDF</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="PDF">

Export to PortableDocFormat (PDF) is a page-based export type. This export retains both layout and formatting options, so the exported report will display as it displayed on the Preview screen. PDFdocuments cannot be altered without specialized software, making this format useful if you want to email the report or save it for later viewing.

<div class="example">

**Example:** PortableDocFormat

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="RPTR">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Report Definition (RPTR)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="RPTR">

This is a special Crystal-specific export format that generates a read-only version of the RPT file. The data, report definitions and database connection are exported. This file can only be opened from the Crystal Report Viewer. This protects the report from accidental modification. The report cannot be modified, and a new RPT file cannot be created from this file.

This export retains connection to the database, so if the report is refreshed, this file will be updated.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="TXT">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Text (TXT)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="TXT">

This exports the report in plain text. This option does not retain any formatting information.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="WORD">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Microsoft Word</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="WORD">

This option exports the report in Microsoft Word format. The text and drawing objects of the original report are retained.

<div class="example">

**Example:** WordForWindows

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="XML">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />XML</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="XML">

This option exports the report in an XML format. This uses the SAP Crystal Reports XML schema for the export. This option is usually used for data exchange.

</div>
